content.page_summary: Guidance on revascularization strategies for patients with acute myocardial infarction (MI) complicated by cardiogenic shock (CS) and for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients with multivessel disease (MVD). Reviews randomized trials (SHOCK, CULPRIT-SHOCK) and offers recommendations for immediate management and peri‑operative considerations for emergency CABG.

findings: Approximately 60% had anterior MI (text shows malformed characters; interpreted as ~60%).
Among patients assigned to emergency revascularization, 64% underwent PCI and 36% underwent CABG.
At 6 months, mortality was lower in the group assigned to revascularization compared with initial medical therapy.
SHOCK_trial.recommendation_from_evidence: Immediate coronary angiography and PCI if feasible in patients with acute MI complicated by CS. If coronary anatomy unsuitable for PCI, emergency CABG is recommended.

CULPRIT-SHOCK_trial.population_note: Included ACS patients with cardiogenic shock, both with and without ST‑segment elevation (or equivalent).
CULPRIT-SHOCK_trial.epidemiology: Nearly 80% of ACS patients with CS have multivessel disease (MVD).
CULPRIT-SHOCK_trial.intervention_finding: PCI during the index procedure should be restricted to the infarct‑related artery (IRA) only.
outcomes: IRA‑only PCI was associated with a significant reduction in the composite of all‑cause death or renal replacement therapy at 30‑day follow‑up (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71–0.96).
At 1‑year follow‑up, mortality did not differ significantly between the IRA‑only and multivessel PCI groups.

ACS_with_CS_and_MVD: Restrict PCI during the index procedure to the infarct‑related artery (IRA) only (based on CULPRIT‑SHOCK findings).
Consider staged or complete revascularization later when appropriate, guided by patient stability and anatomy.
emergency_CABG: For patients undergoing emergency CABG, consider appropriate peri‑operative strategies (including prophylactic or on‑demand mechanical circulatory support) based on pre‑operative clinical status (age, comorbidities, electrical instability, extent of jeopardized myocardium, duration of ischemia from symptom onset, right ventricular involvement, and technical/logistical feasibility).

figure.description: Algorithm for management of ACS patients undergoing PCI of the infarct‑related artery (IRA) with an angiographically significant stenosis in ≥1 non‑IRA. Diagram differentiates pathways for cardiogenic shock, STEMI, and NSTE‑ACS and shows recommendations for immediate IRA‑only PCI, staged complete revascularization, or complete revascularization depending on presentation.
